raw_case_text:
A 51-year-old female patient presented to our medical center with complaints of altered sensorium, fever, and chills for the past five days, and dyspnea for the past two days.
A general examination revealed an average build, with the patient being moderately nourished. She was febrile with a body temperature of 100 F, and had a pulse rate of 128 bpm, blood pressure of 100/70 mmHg on inotrope, 94% SpO2, and respiration rate of 24 cycles/minute; dehydration was also noted. Positive findings included fever, tachycardia, hypotension, dehydration, tachypnea, and hypoxia.
During the systemic evaluation, on the central nervous system (CNS) examination, the patient exhibited signs of lethargy, irritability, noncompliance with verbal instructions, and movement of all four limbs. There was no neck stiffness. Kernig and Brudzinski signs were negative. Bilateral pupils reacted similarly to light. Bilateral extensor plantar reflex was noted. On respiratory examination, bilateral fine basal crepitations were present. On per abdominal examination, mild hepatomegaly was noted.
We investigated dengue, Leptospira, malaria, typhoid, and rickettsia, which are common causes of acute febrile illness with associated altered sensorium and mild-to-severe hepatic impairment. Day 1 reports (Tables 1, 2) suggested dengue and Leptospira coinfection fever with mild hepatitis and thrombocytopenia. Fluid resuscitation was started with crystalloids for dehydration and injection. Doxycycline 100 mg twice a day is given intravenously to treat leptospirosis.
MRI of the brain (Figure 1) and CSF studies were conducted, both of which showed viral encephalitis changes.
In addition to two episodes of melena, there was worsening of the patient's thrombocytopenia, and the development of ecchymosis over both the upper and lower limbs occurred on day 3 (Figures 2A-2C). Furthermore, there was a great deal of subcutaneous edema on the front side of the left elbow and the area immediately around the forearm, as well as fluid-filled vesicles (bullae) all over the left upper limb (Figure 2D); the patient was transfused with single-donor platelets, fresh frozen plasma, and packed red blood cells.
An endotracheal intubation was performed on the patient immediately after she experienced respiratory distress on day 6, and mechanical ventilator support was started at the same time.
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax was performed, which revealed bilateral pleural effusion and ground-glass opacities in the superior segment of the right lower lobe with interlobular septal thickening in the left lower lobe (Figures 3A-3C), suggestive of pulmonary edema. An undiluted infusion of furosemide 200 mg injection was started. The patient was kept on mechanical ventilation while arterial blood gases (Table 3) and other laboratory data were examined (Tables 1, 3).
The patient was taken off the mechanical ventilator, and a T-piece experiment was performed before extubation. The patient was transferred to the ward for observation and then discharged. The follow-up went smoothly.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 51-year-old female presenting with altered sensorium, fever, and chills for 5 days, and dyspnea for 2 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 5 days prior to admission with high fever, chills, and progressive confusion and altered sensorium, followed 2 days prior to presentation by worsening dyspnea. Following admission, she developed two episodes of melena, worsening severe thrombocytopenia, diffuse ecchymoses across both upper and lower extremities on day 3, massive subcutaneous edema of the left forearm and elbow, and extensive fluid-filled bullae over the left upper extremity. On hospital day 6, she developed acute respiratory failure requiring emergent endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: body temperature 100 °F, pulse rate 128 beats/min, blood pressure 100/70 mmHg on inotropic support, SpO2 94%, respiratory rate 24 cycles/min. General: average build, moderately nourished, clinically dehydrated. CNS: lethargic, irritable, noncompliant with verbal instructions, moving all four extremities; no neck stiffness; Kernig and Brudzinski signs negative; bilateral pupils equally reactive to light; bilateral extensor plantar reflex (Babinski sign positive). Respiratory: bilateral fine basal crepitations. Abdomen: mild hepatomegaly on palpation. Skin/Extremities: worsening ecchymoses over upper and lower extremities, massive subcutaneous edema on anterior left elbow and forearm, and fluid-filled bullae throughout the left upper extremity.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory evaluation revealed severe thrombocytopenia, mild hepatitis with elevated transaminases, and arterial blood gas abnormalities consistent with hypoxemic respiratory compromise.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI: signal changes consistent with viral encephalitis. Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: findings demonstrating viral encephalitis changes. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax: bilateral pleural effusion and ground-glass opacities in the superior segment of the right lower lobe with interlobular septal thickening in the left lower lobe, consistent with pulmonary edema.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Coinfection of Leptospira and Dengue virus presenting as acute febrile illness with meningoencephalitis, acute pulmonary edema / respiratory distress, severe hemorrhagic diathesis (melena, limb ecchymoses, cutaneous bullae), mild hepatitis, and severe thrombocytopenia. Confirmed by positive diagnostic testing on Day 1 for both Leptospira and Dengue. Differential diagnoses of malaria, typhoid fever, and rickettsial infection were systematically investigated and excluded.
Plan & Treatment: Emergent fluid resuscitation with IV crystalloids for dehydration; inotropic blood pressure support; intravenous doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for leptospirosis; transfusions of single-donor platelets, fresh frozen plasma, and packed red blood cells; invasive mechanical ventilation; and continuous undiluted intravenous infusion of furosemide 200 mg for pulmonary edema.
Outcome: Successful weaning and extubation following T-piece trial; complete stabilization and resolution of organ dysfunction; transferred to general ward and discharged home with uneventful follow-up.
